verses.1: And Ahaz reported to Isaiah everything that Eliyahhu had done, and everything he had done to all the prophets in Harzeel.
verses.2: And Eizbel sent an angel to Elijah, saying, “Do this: God will do this. Soon, I will put your soul into one of them’s body.”
verses.3: And he saw, and he stood up. Then he went to his tent. He entered the city of Yehuda, and he placed his young man there.
verses.4: And he went into the desert, along the shore. He arrived and sat down under one of the trees. He asked his soul for death. He said, “Lord, now take my soul away, for it is not good for me to remain among my ancestors.”
verses.5: And he lay down under one of the branches. Then, this angel touched him and said to him, “Get up, Echol.”
verses.6: And behold, from his mouth came smoke and water. He ate, drank, sat down, and then lay down.
verses.7: And the angel of the LORD sat down again, and he touched him. Then he said, “Arise, eat; for there is plenty of food for you.”
verses.8: And he ate, drank, and walked with the strength that came from eating. This lasted for forty days and forty nights, until he reached Mount God.
verses.9: And he went there into the cave. There, he saw what God had shown him. And God said to him, “What are you doing here, Elihu?”
verses.10: And he said, “I long for Jehovah, the God of hosts! For the sons of Israel have abandoned your covenant. They have destroyed your idols and killed your prophets in Babylon and Jerusalem. I am alone, and they are seeking to take my life.”
verses.11: And he said, “Go and stand on the mountain before Jehovah. Then you will see Jehovah coming forth, with a great and powerful spirit, who can break through mountains and split rocks apart. It isn’t a cloud of Jehovah; after that comes a noise, but it isn’t the noise of Jehovah.”
verses.12: And after the noise of the fire, there was no fire from Jehovah. And after the fire, there was a loud, faint cry.
verses.13: And when Eliyahu heard this, his face turned red with anger. He rushed out and stood at the entrance of the cave. There, he heard a voice saying, “What are you doing here, Eliyahu?”
verses.14: And he said, “I long for Jehovah, the God of hosts. For the sons of Israel have abandoned your covenant. They have destroyed your idols and killed your prophets in Babylon and Eder. I am alone, and they are seeking to take my life away from me.”
verses.15: And the LORD said to him, “Go back along your path from the desert of Dammishah. Then you will go and destroy Chedorhela, king of Aram.”
verses.16: And Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, will be made king over Israel. And Elijah, son of Saphat, who was born from a sick and dying mother, will be made prophet under you.
verses.17: And the one who is hidden from Hazael will die; Jehu will also die. And the one who is hidden from Jehu will die as well, Elisha.
verses.18: And I remained in Israel for seven thousand years. All the blessings that were not given to the owner, and all the promises that were not fulfilled.
verses.19: And he went there, and found Eliezer, the son of Shaphat. He was working on two dozen beams before him. In those two dozen beams, Elijah went to him and threw Adar to him.
verses.20: And he left the morning and rushed after Eliyah. He said, “Please help my father and mother. I will go with you.” But Eliyah replied, “Go back, for what have I done to you?”
verses.21: And he sat down beside him. He took the bread in the morning, offered it as an offering, and ate it with all its bread. Then he gave it to the people to eat. After that, he got up and went after Elijah.
